transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-12
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Dana Lee (Orchid CISO), Mark Lyons (Orchid Head of Cloud Ops), Janelle Park (Orchid Compliance)

[00:00] Ava: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Ava from Redwood, this is Ravi, our solutions engineer. We're here to walk through Redwood's SOC 2 and ISO27001 posture and get a sense of Orchid's requirements. Can each of you quickly intro?
[00:15] Dana: Hi, Dana Lee, CISO at Orchid. Thanks. We're primarily validating controls for PHI, so thinking about data residency, encryption, auditability.
[00:28] Mark: Mark Lyons, cloud ops. We'll be focused on networking, VPC, and deployment modes.
[00:35] Janelle: Janelle Park, compliance. I'll be shepherding the evidence requests.
[00:40] Ava: Great. Quick agenda: trust center access and artifacts, controls mapping, SSO/RBAC, audit logs, KMS/encryption, and next steps. Does that sound good?
[00:52] Dana: Yep. Also timeline — we're aiming for vendor review complete by end of May.
[01:03] Ava: Understood. We'll try to be concise.
[01:20] Ravi: I'll start with a high-level. Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 certified controls. We host both an online Trust Center with downloadable reports and a controls mapping spreadsheet that maps our org controls to ISO/SOC criteria.
[01:35] Dana: Is the Trust Center publicly accessible or do you gate it? We need access to the reports — ideally read-only link or SSO.
[01:47] Ava: Good question. We can grant Trust Center access via SSO — we support SAML. Most customers get a scoped read-only portal. We'll send a link and invite.
[01:59] Mark: When you say SAML, do you support IdP-initiated flows and SCIM? We want group sync and RBAC integration.
[02:12] Ravi: We support SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. Our RBAC is role-based with customizable roles for admin, auditor, ops. Group sync via SCIM is supported. There was one minor early quirk with some IdPs where attribute mapping needed tweaking, but in practice customers get it done during onboarding.
[02:36] Janelle: And audit logs — retention and export?
[02:42] Ava: We retain full audit logs for API and console activity for 365 days by default for enterprise tier, with longer retention as an add-on. Logs include user, action, timestamp, and request metadata. Exports available to S3 or via streaming to your SIEM.
[02:57] Dana: Is there any sampling or filtering? For compliance we need full fidelity.
[03:04] Ravi: For enterprise customers we do full fidelity; no sampling. We can set up streaming to your Splunk/Datadog/Kafka as part of on-boarding.
[03:15] Dana: Good. Let's talk about data residency and PHI. We need to ensure all PHI stored in US-only regions and contractually bound.
[03:25] Ava: Redwood supports pinned regional deployment. For hosted API, you can pin region or choose Dedicated or Private deployment for stronger guarantees. Our Private deployment offers customer-managed networking and on-prem packaging for regulated environments.
[03:40] Mark: When you say pinned region, is that soft routing preference or a hard guarantee?
[03:45] Ravi: For hosted, pinned region is a hard affinity — requests are routed to capacity in that region, but we do keep a fallback policy for availability. For contractual data residency for PHI we recommend Dedicated or Private, where isolation is stronger and data-at-rest stays within customer region and storage buckets under customer account if requested.
[04:05] Janelle: Does Redwood support contract language for data processing addendum and subprocessor list?
[04:11] Ava: Yes, DPA and a current subprocessor list are provided. We'll share the DPA draft in Trust Center and can negotiate standard clauses.
[04:20] Mark: Encryption — we're using KMS at the moment. Can Redwood integrate with our KMS/HSM?
[04:27] Ravi: Yes. For Dedicated and Private, we support customer-managed KMS via AWS KMS or a bring-your-own-HSM model. For hosted, we offer envelope encryption with customer-managed keys in some tiers; on enterprise plan we can arrange BYOK via AWS KMS or GCP KMS; HSM support is available for private deployments.
[04:45] Dana: Is key rotation under our control?
[04:48] Ava: For BYOK, key rotation policies remain with your KMS. For Redwood-managed keys we rotate per industry best practices and provide attestation and KMS access logs.
[04:58] Mark: Do you publish KMS usage or crypto primitives used? AES256, RSA?
[05:05] Ravi: We use industry-standard AES-256 for data-at-rest and TLS 1.2+/1.3 for in-transit. For envelope encryption we use AES-GCM where supported. We'll send a diagram of the crypto flow and an HSM options doc.
[05:20] Janelle: Controls mapping — we need a spreadsheet that maps our control IDs to Redwood controls and evidence artifacts so our auditors can validate.
[05:31] Ava: We maintain a controls matrix that maps SOC 2/ISO controls to Redwood's processes and evidence. We will share a CSV/XLSX version and highlight any gaps that would require customer-side compensating controls.
[05:44] Dana: Any known gaps for PHI customers we should be aware of?
[05:50] Ravi: The main consideration is that hosted multi-tenant environments require contractual and configuration guards — if you need strict isolation, Dedicated/Private is recommended. Also for logs/sensitive data storage, we can store logs in your account for extra separation.
[06:08] Mark: About audit logs again — can we get real-time streaming into our Splunk with guaranteed ordering?
[06:15] Ravi: We can stream logs to customers' S3 or to a syslog/Kafka endpoint. Ordering is best-effort but you can rely on timestamp indexing. For strict ordering we recommend ingesting with a sequence id we include in payloads.
[06:31] Ava: On the topic of attestations, our SOC 2 Type II report covers the period Oct 2024 — Apr 2025. Our ISO27001 certificate was issued March 2024 and is current. We will provide redacted report PDFs and the certificate via the Trust Center invite.
[06:50] Dana: Will the SOC report include results of penetration tests or is that separate?
[06:55] Ravi: The SOC 2 report references vulnerability management and the pen test cadence; full pen test reports are typically not included in SOC but we can provide executive summaries and - in some cases - redacted pen-test reports under an NDA.
[07:08] Janelle: Do you have SOC 2 coverage for subservices / subprocessors? We use a third-party key management vendor.
[07:16] Ava: We publish our subprocessor list and indicate which subprocessors have their own attestations. For customer-managed KMS we can avoid Redwood-managed subprocessors.
[07:26] Mark: How do you handle access reviews and RBAC enforcement? We need quarterly reviews and ability to revoke quickly.
[07:33] Ravi: We support role-based policies and an admin console for access revocation. We also provide audit logs for IAM changes and can run periodic access reports for review. We support scheduled access reviews via the console or via API.
[07:47] Dana: Do you have CIS benchmarks or hardened images for dedicated nodes?
[07:52] Ravi: Yes, Dedicated nodes are provisioned from hardened images and we can provide the build recipes and baseline configs. For private/on-prem we provide a deployment guide with hardening steps.
[08:05] Ava: Any questions on incident response?
[08:08] Dana: We're interested in timeframe SLA for incident notification and forensic artifacts.
[08:13] Ravi: We have an incident response playbook; customers are notified according to our SLA — typically initial notification within one hour for sev-1, detailed postmortem within the agreed timeframe. We preserve forensic logs and can provide exports under your request.
[08:28] Janelle: Regarding retention and deletion, can customers request full data deletion and get attestation?
[08:34] Ava: Yes, deletion requests are supported. For hosted customers we provide deletion workflows and a certificate of deletion. For Dedicated/Private, you control storage and can perform deletion directly.
[08:44] Mark: A quick note on latency vs cost — if we move to Dedicated for PHI, what's the delta in cost and what are the perf guarantees?
[08:54] Ravi: Dedicated is higher cost due to reserved GPU capacity, but gives predictable throughput and better isolation. Our Dedicated SLAs include uptime and latency SLOs and we can share typical perf numbers for models and sequence lengths in the controls pack.
[09:08] Dana: For our procurement, we'll need to see the subprocessor list, SOC 2 PDF, ISO cert, DPA, and the controls matrix.
[09:16] Ava: We'll bundle those in the Trust Center link. Expect an invite after this call.
[09:23] Mark: For the controls matrix, can you indicate where Orchid will need to provide evidence? For example, network segmentation in our VPC.
[09:31] Ravi: We'll highlight customer responsibilities in the matrix — e.g., network ACLs, VPC peering setup, and your Key Management controls if BYOK is chosen.
[09:40] Janelle: One small practical: our auditors want a list of accounts with console access as of a date. Can you produce that?
[09:47] Ava: Yes, we can produce a snapshot export of accounts and roles for a specified date. We'll deliver that as an evidence artifact.
[09:56] Dana: Perfect. Timeline recap?
[10:00] Ava: We'll: 1) send Trust Center invite and SOC/ISO artifacts by 2025-05-15. 2) Share controls mapping CSV by 2025-05-19. 3) Schedule VPC deep-dive for week of 2025-05-26. Anything to add?
[10:12] Mark: Please include HSM options doc when you send the KMS info.
[10:17] Ravi: Will do.
[10:20] Janelle: And please flag any evidence that will require an NDA for redacted pen test reports.
[10:25] Ava: Noted.
[10:30] Dana: Thanks, that covers it from our side.
[10:34] Ava: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts.
[10:40] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hears (e.g., "K-V cash" for KV cache; "Redwood Dedicate" instead of Dedicated in auto-transcript) were left as-is.
